findings.description: The user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY as plaintext static IAM credentials. User data is retrievable via the instance metadata service (including through SSRF against the internet-facing web server) and is persisted in cleartext in the EC2 API and Terraform state.

The instance is launched into a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch = true, with a default route to an internet gateway and a security group allowing 0.0.0.0/0 on TCP/22 and TCP/80, making it directly reachable from the internet including on the SSH administrative port.

No metadata_options block sets http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled. Combined with the plaintext credentials in user data and a publicly reachable Apache server, this creates a direct SSRF-to-credential-theft path.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is declared, so the root EBS volume may be created unencrypted depending on the AMI and account-level default, leaving data at rest unprotected.
Ingress permits TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet and enabling credential brute-force and exploitation of the SSH service.

Ingress permits TCP/80 from 0.0.0.0/0 and no TLS listener or HTTPS ingress is configured anywhere in the stack, so all web traffic to the host is transmitted in cleartext and open to interception or tampering.
The egress rule allows all protocols to all ports for 0.0.0.0/0, giving a compromised host unconstrained outbound connectivity for data exfiltration and command-and-control.

The EBS volume is created without encrypted = true (the attribute is explicitly commented out), so data written to the volume attached to the web host is stored unencrypted and not protected by KMS key access control.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and therefore persists an unencrypted copy of the data that can be copied, shared with other accounts, or restored elsewhere without KMS protection.
The VPC flow log bucket declares no server_side_encryption_configuration, so network telemetry revealing internal addressing, topology, and traffic patterns is stored without enforced encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, ACL restriction, or bucket policy is defined for the flow log bucket, leaving sensitive network log data exposed to accidental public ACL or policy grants.
No bucket policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false is attached, so flow log objects can be read or written over unencrypted HTTP connections.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true, combined with the route table association carrying a 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway, causes every instance launched here to be internet-facing by default, removing the network boundary.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true with an internet-gateway default route makes any instance launched in this subnet directly reachable from the internet by default.

No aws_default_security_group resource is declared to strip the VPC default security group's rules, so it retains allow-all intra-group ingress and unrestricted egress for any resource that attaches to it implicitly.
